body:
A non-zero exit isn't one kind of failure, and several kinds can be told apart without a model. A cheap deterministic first pass makes fix on failure (#17) and `?why` (#14) better, and it's easy to test.

**Classes**
| Exit | Meaning | Response |
|---|---|---|
| 127 | command not found | Suggest the package that provides it (local apt data); no model needed for the common case |
| 126 | found but not executable | Permission or noexec; say so |
| 130 (128+2) | interrupted by Ctrl-C | Not an error; offer nothing |
| 128+n | killed by signal n | Name the signal (e.g. 137 = SIGKILL, often the OOM killer) |
| sudo failure | wrong password or not in sudoers | **Never** offer a retry or anything that touches the password; just say what happened (ADR-0006) |
| other non-zero | command-specific | Pass to the quarantined reader (M0.11) for a diagnosis |

The exit code and the gate's parse of the command are trusted, so this pass needs no taint. Only the stderr text is untrusted.

**Done when**
- A table-driven test covers each class.
- Ctrl-C triggers no correction offer.
- A sudo authentication failure produces no correction that re-runs sudo automatically.
- Only the "other" class reaches the reader.

---
**Design review 2026-10-14** (#63)

Exit codes are only trusted when they come from the session's OSC 133 markers with the per-session value (#65); output can't forge them. **Depends on** #65.
title: M0.12 — Classify failures by exit code before asking a model
